items.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018
items.q: I work with people who have worked with ... Paul Simon ... I did an album for Suzanne Vega ... I have: 'Hi Catherine, this is Paul Simon.'

ctx.x: I recently watched a documentary I think called “Twenty Feet From Stardom.” Do all — I suppose I know the answer to this already. Do all or most back-up singers aspire to move up to the front of the stage? © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

No. Because it’s two different sets of skills. So I work with many colleagues who, some of whom have had solo careers, and some have not. And we are very happy backing up whomever we, whatever iconic individuals we get to back up. It’s an honor. It’s a privilege, it’s a great job. You learn all the time. You have to aspire to sing in tune, work with other people, it’s a team effort. You have to move together. And you’re part of a big thing that — people are very happy in the audience you know what I mean? It’s a…
Well said. Because I did get that impression, like that they all didn’t quite feel like they made it.
